title: From Locked Portal to Clean Data
hook: A one-click tool that logs in to a secure, OTP-protected portal, downloads every policy report, and turns the PDFs into clean CSVs

slides.title: From Locked Portal to Clean Data
slides.subtitle: An automated PDF data pipeline for an insurance client
slides.narration: This is a data engineering project for a real client. Divyesh automated a job that used to mean downloading and copying insurance reports by hand.

slides.title: The problem
bullets: The client's policy reports are PDFs inside a secure portal protected by OTP login
Every report had to be downloaded and copied into spreadsheets by hand
This was slow, prone to mistakes, and impossible to keep up to date
The goal: an automated pipeline that produces clean data for a BI dashboard
slides.narration: All the data was locked inside PDF reports in a secure portal, so getting it out meant hours of manual downloading and copying.

slides.title: How the pipeline works

steps.label: Log in
steps.detail: The user signs in once in a real browser, including the OTP. Playwright saves the session for later runs

steps.label: Collect
steps.detail: Playwright searches the policies, pages through the results, opens each policy, generates its report and saves the PDF

steps.label: Extract
steps.detail: pdfplumber and rule-based parsing pull structured fields from each PDF, detecting Life or General policy layouts

steps.label: Store
steps.detail: Each policy number gets one CSV row, so re-runs update rows instead of adding duplicates

slides.narration: A person handles only the secure login. After that, the pipeline browses the portal, collects every report, reads each one, and keeps the data organised.

slides.title: What gets extracted
bullets: Life policies: coverage amounts, status, premium schedule, owner and insured details
General policies: deposits, withdrawals, market value, maturity date and owner contact details
Handles more than one layout for the same field, and validates that required fields are present
slides.narration: Every report becomes one clean row, with up to nineteen fields per policy, and the dataset never contains duplicates.

slides.title: Built for non-technical users
bullets: A Streamlit app with three buttons: Login, Refresh New Policies, and Re-Check All
Incremental mode skips policies already downloaded, while a full re-check rebuilds everything
Download all the PDFs and CSVs as one timestamped ZIP
A one-click Windows launcher sets up the environment and starts the app
slides.narration: The client doesn't need to know any Python. They click a button, and the data refreshes.

slides.title: Security and reliability
bullets: No credentials in code: the password and OTP are entered by a person in the browser
Session files, settings and all extracted data are kept out of git
An expired session is detected, and the app prompts the user to log in again
pytest runs on generated sample PDFs in GitHub Actions on every push
slides.narration: Because this touches personal financial data, security came first. Nothing sensitive goes into the code or the repository, and automated tests check the extraction on every change.

slides.title: Lessons and what's next
bullets: Biggest lesson: real-world PDFs have many layouts, so the parsing rules need fallbacks and validation
Next: feed the CSVs into an interactive BI dashboard for ongoing monitoring
The code, tests and synthetic sample data are on GitHub
slides.narration: The trickiest part was that the same field could appear in different places across reports. The code and sample data are on GitHub, so you can explore it yourself.
